newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end quiet day mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end quiet day mostly higher.

text.p: IMM currency futures at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange ended mostly higher, with June marks and Swiss francs near session highs.
Traders said concerns over possible EMU delays buoyed the mark, with long dollar profit-taking aiding currency gains.
But traders said action was extremely quiet to start out the week, with rangebound trade likely through midweek.

Currencies "look like they could be turning," one IMM trading floor manager said. "This week will be a very good indicator by Wednesday or Thursday and we'll see if the bullish dollar move will last much longer," he said.
But overall, he said world interest rate differentials still make the dollar "the best bet."
Others said marks and Swiss were due for an uptick after so many weeks of plumbing the lows.
"It was good to see the mark finally higher," a currency futures trader said. "I haven't seen the marks on the plus side in a long time."

He said yen futures trade was very quiet and choppy, with June remaining within its recent range. June has traded within a $0.008290 to $0.008397 band for five sessions. It settled near the middle of that zone on Monday.
One futures analyst said Tuesday's trade could be pivotal for the rest of the week.
"If I'm right, this dollar should start rallying now because we've had our two days of dips," he said.
"The dollar on the chart looks overbought but fundamentally I think we're going to go higher in the dollar and lower in the currencies," he said.
Some currency action on Monday was tied to rolling of positions from March into June, because June took lead contract status on Monday.

At the close, June yen was up $0.000015 at $0.008334, marks gained $0.0050 to $0.5914, Swiss francs rose $0.0044 to $0.6865, sterling rose $0.0020 to $1.6012, Can dollar lost $0.0010 to $0.7344, Aussie dollar rose $0.0010 at $0.7875, Mexican peso rose $0.000275 to $0.120125.
